### J-1 No contract renders the agents, and the skill loses its `nio agents sync`
- quote: "plan the gate, render the agents and write each planned lens's pack to `.nio/runs/<run>/jury/packs/<lens>.md`"
- quote: "Start a run with `nio run`, and run `nio agents sync` so every `nio-<lens>` agent exists."
- quote: "steps 2–5 and 8 become one loop: plan and add your own triggers (`nio jury plan`, `nio pack`, `--add`), then run `nio jury next <slug> <gate> [--add ...]`"
- situation (architecture-fit): today step 2 of the skill runs `agents.sync` before any juror starts. CT-1's shape only "calls `collect` and `check` in turn", and CT-2 only writes packs and step.json. Neither calls `agents.sync`, and CT-6 folds step 2 into the loop without keeping the sync. CT-5 changes every juror card to `tools: [read, write]`, so a project whose `.claude/agents/nio-*.md` were rendered before this change keeps read-only jurors. Those jurors can't write the output file the pack asks for, so the orchestrator has to save each answer again or the gate stalls on `no output`.
- fix: in CT-1 case 2, call `agents.sync(root)` before writing packs (and refuse on its errors), or keep `nio agents sync` as a named step in CT-6's loop. Add a TC asserting that the rendered juror files grant Write after a step.
- validation: confirmed: FR-12 (spec.md:104) says the step renders the agents, but CT-1 (it calls only `collect` and `check`), CT-2 (writes packs and step.json) and CT-6 (folds step 2 into the loop) never call `agents.sync`. Cards already rendered read-only stay read-only after CT-5 changes the juror cards.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-1 case 2 calls agents.sync first (FR-12 already says so); TC-12 asserts the rendered nio-logic grants Write

### J-2 The escalation `next:` always uses a `fixcheck --blocker` pack, and its output file is named in no pack
- quote: "next: escalate <lens>: run 2 more jurors on nio jury fixcheck <slug> <gate> --lens <lens> --blocker J-n, outputs <gate>-<lens>-2.md and <gate>-<lens>-3.md"
- quote: "each with a fresh pack (after the first review, the blocker's pack, `nio jury fixcheck <slug> spec --lens <lens> --blocker J-<n>`)"
- quote: "Write your whole output to the file your pack names, and to no other file; never edit the files you judge."
- situation (architecture-fit): the skill, which CT-6 says keeps escalation, gives first-review escalation jurors a fresh first-review pack and uses the `--blocker` pack only after the first review. CT-1 sends every escalation to the `--blocker` pack. That pack is built from `fixcheck`'s lines, which name no output file, and the step doesn't write it. So under CT-5's card sentence the juror has no file to write. The first-review pack the step does write (`packs/<lens>.md`) names `<gate>-<lens>.md`, so reusing it would overwrite the original juror's output.
- fix: have CT-1 pick the pack by phase, as the skill does. Have the step (CT-2) write `packs/<lens>-2.md` and `packs/<lens>-3.md`, each ending with the `## Your output` line for its `-2`/`-3` file, or explicitly assign this to the orchestrator in CT-6.
- validation: confirmed: CT-1's escalation `next:` always points at `nio jury fixcheck ... --blocker`, but skill step 5 uses that pack only after the first review. CT-2 writes no `-2`/`-3` pack and appends no `## Your output` line to a fixcheck pack, so under CT-5's card sentence the escalation juror has no output file named.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-1 escalation line: the orchestrator copies the right pack per phase with the -2/-3 output line; escalation stays the skill's

### J-4 The escalation trigger counts jurors the ledger keeps across rounds
- quote: "a lens with a confirmed open blocker and fewer than 3 jurors of that lens"
- quote: "juror = led["jurors"].setdefault(path.stem, {"attempts": 0})"
- situation (architecture-fit): `merge` keys jurors by file stem and never removes them, so `spec-logic-2` and `spec-logic-3` stay in `led["jurors"]` after the first escalation. In a later re-review where the refuter confirms a new blocker from logic, CT-1 sees 3 jurors of that lens, skips escalation, and composes the outcome. The skill's step 5 escalates every confirmed blocker.
- fix: count only the lens's jurors whose `round` is the current round (or that judged this blocker), and add a TC for a second escalation in a later round.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-1 counts only the lens's jurors of the current round

### J-5 TC-19 expects an outcome line that CT-1 and TC-1 say the step never prints with a batch pending
- quote: "the step prints the same `outcome:` line as the hand-run check, writes no second verdict record, and its `next:` line is the refuter action (the batch still pending)."

Separately, the hand-run `check` composes `pending`, which is never recorded, so "writes no second verdict record" holds whatever the step does.

The step therefore prints no `outcome:` line, which contradicts TC-19's "same `outcome:` line" and agrees with TC-1's "no outcome line".
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-19 asserts no outcome line while the batch is pending; the no-second-record check moved to TC-2's rejected state
